pr_body:
* Support passing additional attributes to the import map Component
  * This allows passing a nonce for Content Security Policies.
* Fix an issue with the paths on the integrity attribute not being valid relative links.
  * This caused certain importmap entries to be ignored.
* Fixes the Blazor United Sample.

Fixes #57277

issue_context.title: Add a new parameter to the ImportMap component that allows to specify a Nonce for the importmap html script
comments:
Wow, that was fast! Thanks.

I'm using [NetEscapades.AspNetCore.SecurityHeaders](https://github.com/andrewlock/NetEscapades.AspNetCore.SecurityHeaders) so I thought to simply apply the Nonce created by the library. 
I like your approach better though, I'll see if I can integrate it with the library.

Thanks again!

I got a working hack but I had to steal the internal [ToJson](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Components/Endpoints/src/Assets/ImportMapDefinition.cs#L206) method code and change the [JsonSerializerOptions](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/1df67c0c8bf3e31ea6fc25308c40cb76367ba8a1/src/Components/Endpoints/src/Assets/ImportMapSerializerContext.cs#L15) adding `NewLine = "\n"` in order to have a valid sha (I'm on Windows).

I'm a bit on the fence about asking, because probably using a Nonce is simply easier, but do you think it could be doable to expose the JsonSerializerOptions so I could simply clone it adding the NewLine specification?

@ghidello you can call `ToString` https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Components/Endpoints/src/Assets/ImportMapDefinition.cs#L213 as a proxy and you avoid calling ToJson.

I'm not opposed to changing our internal options to use a different line ending, but I have to think for a split second about it, since I don't like the idea of potentially mixing line endings on a page.

In any case, you can handle the serialization yourself if you want to have full control over it, it's like 3 lines of code.

Finally, IMO using a hash with CSP is better because it offers a stronger guarantee that the content is what you expected. I only recommend using nonce as a last resort and author/architect your app to avoid it where possible (for example no "dynamic" inline scripts)
I don't know how I missed the `ToString` method. Sorry! Thanks again.

> Finally, IMO using a hash with CSP is better because it offers a stronger guarantee that the content is what you expected.

If you can't calculate the expected value ahead of time, and instead need to calculate it at runtime by serializing the `ImportMapDefinition`, then I don't see how that adds any stronger guarantee? 🤔 Essentially you're allowing "whatever is in the import map definition" in both cases, the hash is just more expensive to calculate, no? 😄
